title: What a Colab GPU holds for A8's two candidate models
summary: Peak GPU memory and time per batch for the 11.7M and 56.4M Transformers, measured by Coulson in Colab on 2026-09-28 with scripts/colab_memory_probe.py, in two separate sessions. Task #118. The question it answers: whether memory, the one objection left, rules out the larger model for A8.

config.optimizer: AdamW, three full training steps (forward, backward, step)
config.worst_case: every sentence in the batch at the stated length

lengths.180: roughly the same sentences as SentencePiece pieces in A9, about 1.8x longer

vocabularies.8000: SentencePiece, as the benchmark and A9 use
vocabularies.50000: a large word-level vocabulary, as the A8 notebook's NMTDataset builds

caveats: The first row's time in each session is the GPU's first call, not a cost of that configuration: the same model at the longer length runs far faster in the next row.
Both sessions drew the same A100. Whether a student's session can draw a smaller GPU is not measured here; the T4 and L4 columns use nominal capacities, not measurements.
Every sentence at the cap is the worst case. Real batches are shorter, and the A8 notebook's length bucketing makes most of them much shorter.
Memory only. Whether the 56.4M model is worth its time is the question the a8-benchmark report answers, in its capacity table.
